status: DRAFT. Estimable: discontinuation_handling resolved 2026-08-18. Remaining open items are data-quality tolerances, not design blockers.
_why_this_file: The design decisions are encoded here rather than only in prose so that they are
diffable, hashable, and readable by the build scripts. This file is the
definition_version source for the provenance block stamped on every shareable
TREAT THIS AS A PROTOCOL, NOT A TUNING FILE. Changing a value here changes what
is being estimated. It is not the place to make a failing run pass. Every edit
should be a deliberate, reviewed commit that also bumps definition_version.

exposure._node_statistic_why: Time-weighted mean of delivered dose over the CRRT records charted inside each 24h node, with charted zero-dose intervals included in both numerator and denominator, and NO imputation for uncharted gaps. Formula: sum(dose_h) / n_charted_hours over the node. REASON 1, consistency with the exposure: this study's exposure is DELIVERED dose (see _prescribed_vs_delivered). Downtime is precisely what makes delivered dose fall below prescribed, so excluding zero-dose intervals would quietly revert the exposure to prescribed intensity. REASON 2, external precedent at the same institution: Quickfall et al., Blood Purif 2026;55:197-209 (references/Koyner_antibiotics_crrt.pdf) computes delivered CRRT dose from hourly effluent flow rates averaged within patient, retains short interruptions such as filter changes and procedures because they are genuinely delivered dose, and excludes gaps >=48h rather than zero-filling them. Within a 24h node a >=48h gap cannot occur, so their rule reduces to 'use what is charted'. SUPERSEDES the earlier windowed_median choice. That choice was justified by the archived MSM's charting-lag artefact, but the objection was measured 2026-08-18 and does not survive a 24h node: hour 0 medians 21.5 mL/kg/hr against 33.5 at every subsequent hour, yet spread over ~24 hourly values it moves the mean by only -0.63 (p95 3.71) versus -0.02 for the median. Bounded, and under a delivered-dose exposure a genuinely slower first hour is signal rather than noise. SENSITIVITY: rerun with the median, and rerun dropping hour 0.
exposure._denominator_caveat: A fixed delta is a different absolute effluent change in every patient, against a fluid-overloaded actual weight. Known to matter: actual-vs-IBW moves the >=30 share from 46% to 76%. Open question 4 in the findings.
exposure._prescribed_vs_delivered: This is DELIVERED dose. RENAL and ATN randomised PRESCRIPTION. A policy defined on delivered dose is not directly implementable; this is a stated limitation, and it is sharper for an intervention estimand than for an association.
exposure._node_statistic_measured: Coordinating site, node 0-24h, 2,144 blocks, 2026-08-18. CRRT charting is hourly and regular (p50 through p95 of the inter-record interval all 1.00h; only 2.0% of gaps exceed 2h), so the time-weighting is well defined and nearly reduces to a simple mean of hourly values. Time-weighted mean: median 33.4, p5 18.6, p95 67.7, max 143.8. Median statistic: median 34.4, max 161.3. Spearman correlation between the two is 0.974, so the dose-response ordering is essentially unchanged; this is a refinement, not a different study. Shiftable fraction at delta=5, floor=15 is 93.3% under the mean against 93.8% under the median, so positivity is not degraded. REJECTED VARIANT: treating uncharted gaps as downtime (denominator = available follow-up hours rather than charted hours). It requires block_discharge_dttm, which is defective: 51 blocks (2.4%) chart more CRRT hours than their discharge timestamp permits, producing doses up to 904 mL/kg/hr. Blocked on todo 2e. It also drops the shiftable fraction to 86.1%.
exposure._node_statistic_site_heterogeneity_RISK: The rule 'include charted zeros, do not impute uncharted gaps' is only as good as a site's downtime charting. At the coordinating site explicit zero-dose records are just 0.6% of the series while 23% of blocks have a gap >6h, so downtime is more often an absence than a charted zero, and the statistic will therefore overstate delivered dose to some degree. A site that charts downtime explicitly and a site that charts nothing will not be measuring the same quantity. MITIGATION: the federated export must carry, per site and per node, the share of node hours charted and the share of charted records at exactly zero, so this is visible in pooling rather than silent.

_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.purpose: Charted-zero versus uncharted-gap is genuinely ambiguous in flowsheet data, so it is pre-specified as a BRACKET rather than a single choice. The three rungs bound the truth from opposite sides and the width of the bracket is itself a reportable per-site diagnostic. Added 2026-08-18 at the user's suggestion.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S1_primary: Denominator = charted hours only. Uncharted gaps excluded entirely. Reads as delivered dose WHILE CHARTED, and is an upper bound on delivered dose. This is the primary, and it is the rung consistent with Quickfall/Koyner, who exclude long gaps rather than zero-filling.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S2: Denominator = first-to-last charted hour inside the node. Gaps INSIDE the observed CRRT span count as downtime at dose 0. Reads as delivered dose OVER THE OBSERVED SPAN. Available now: unlike S3 it never touches block_discharge_dttm.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S3: Denominator = full node follow-up. All uncharted time counts as downtime. Lower bound on delivered dose. BLOCKED on todo 2e: 51 blocks (2.4%) chart more CRRT hours than block_discharge_dttm permits, which produced doses up to 904 mL/kg/hr. Add once 2e is repaired.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.why_S1_and_not_S2_is_primary: Measured 2026-08-18, coordinating site, node 0-24h. Uncharted gaps are NOT random charting lapses: in-hospital mortality falls monotonically with gap length, 73.4% at 0h gap (n=987), 66.0% at 1-2h (n=592), 63.4% at 3-6h (n=361), 52.5% at >6h (n=204); Spearman(gap hours, mortality) = -0.131, p = 1.1e-9. Absence of charting therefore mostly IS downtime, and downtime mostly means the patient is recovering. That vindicates the substantive reading of S2 but disqualifies it as primary, because it pushes recovering patients to a low exposure value by construction and so loads the exposure with recovery status: S2 median falls to 17.9 in the >6h gap group against 29.3 under S1, and Spearman(dose, mortality) rises from +0.219 under S1 to +0.237 under S2. This is confounding by indication amplified by a measurement choice.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.consequence_for_step_02_COVARIATES: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-18, see covariates._volume_assessment_LIMITATION. This key previously required urine output, vasopressors, fluid balance and SOFA in L_t. The urine-output and fluid-balance half of that requirement was inherited from fluid_ARDS, where urine output is a component of the exposure itself, and could not be met by any CLIF site. THE SUBSTANTIVE POINT STANDS AND IS UNCHANGED: the S1/S2 difference is driven by CRRT liberation, liberation tracks renal recovery, and LMTP adjusts for time-varying confounding only to the extent that L_t measures it. What changed is the instrument. The agreed L_t set is in covariates.time_varying_Lt; recovery is now captured only indirectly, through BUN, baseline creatinine and the severity covariates, so the residual confounding on S2 is known in direction and must be reported as such rather than treated as adjusted away.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.agreement: 46.0% of blocks (987 of 2,144) have no uncharted gap in node 0-24h, so S1 and S2 are numerically identical for nearly half the cohort. Gap hours: p50 1, p75 3, p90 6, p95 9, max 20.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.reporting: Report the primary estimate under S1 and the full delta ladder under S2 alongside it. Per site and per node, report the share of node hours charted and the share of charted records at exactly zero, so a site whose downtime charting differs is visible in pooling rather than silent.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.open_alternative_to_bracketing: The bracket could be replaced by an actual discriminator. If a co-charted hourly stream such as vitals is present during a CRRT gap, the patient was being observed and the absence of a CRRT record is more likely genuine downtime than a charting lapse; if nothing at all is charted, the lapse reading is more likely. Not built. Would turn S1/S2 into a single imputed statistic. See todo 1c.

exposure._empty_node_rule_why: A node with NO charted CRRT record at all, in a patient still alive and in hospital, takes exposure 0 and the policy leaves it unshifted. This resolves a collision between two rules that were settled separately: the S1 denominator is 'charted hours only', so an empty node has no defined mean, while discontinuation_handling says liberation is an exposure value of zero. The empty node is the liberation case. Safe for the same reason as the parent decision: 0 - delta < floor for every delta in the ladder, so the policy can never move a patient onto or off therapy. Known cost: a genuinely uncharted node on a still-running machine is misread as liberation. Bounded by the measured finding that absence of charting tracks recovery rather than clerical failure. Decided 2026-08-18.

policy._formula: d(a) = a - delta   if a - delta >= floor;   a   otherwise
policy._critical: NEVER clamp to the floor. The lmtp package supplies no guard for this and will not warn. Clamping breaks the Assumption 5 invertibility condition. See fluid_ARDS/plans/lmtp_discussion.md S4.4 and S4.7.
policy._delta_ladder_why: The ladder IS the dose-response result; report all three rungs, not just the primary. delta=2.5 is universally clean (max binned density ratio 2.6-6.0, zero mass above ratio 10 at any site). delta=10 is the clinically vivid rung but is diluted at two low-dose sites (moves only 23% and 27% of patients) and unstable at the two tight-dosing sites (density ratios to 31.0, 17-70% of cohort above ratio 10). Keep it, with the honest caveat.
policy._floor_why: floor=20 collapses policy coverage to 4% and 11% at the two lowest-dose sites at delta=10, and to 33%/23% even at delta=2.5/5 at one of them. Sensitivity rung only, never primary.

time._tau_why: Retention at 48h is >=38% at every one of the ten sites. A fourth node at 72h is viable at most sites but thin at one (27%). Do not go past tau=4.
time._outcome_grid_why: SIX periods, CHANGED 2026-08-18 from [3, 7, 14, 30]. Exposure runs to day 3 but follow-up runs to day 30, and lmtp requires ONE common time grid: for a survival outcome tau is the number of outcome columns (R/Task.R:125-130), and trt must be of length 1 or exactly tau (R/checks.R:29-40), while cens, compete and time_vary must each be length tau (R/Vars.R:12-18). The previous 4-point grid against 3 exposure nodes was therefore not expressible and failed with "Assertion on 'trt' failed: 'trt' should be of length 1 or 4". Days 1, 2 and 3 are the exposure nodes at 0-24/24-48/48-72h; days 7, 14 and 30 carry the outcome curve past the end of the policy. The grid is still coarsened in the tail so the T x T influence-function covariance stays conditionable at small sites. Full derivation with source citations in docs/lmtp_time_grid_decision.md.
time._exposure_periods_why: The policy intervenes in periods 1-3 ONLY. Periods 4-6 carry an exposure column so the vectors are length tau, but the shift function returns the observed value there. shift is applied one column at a time and receives the column NAME (R/shift.R:39-45, out[[a]] <- .f(data, a)), which is what makes a node-conditional policy expressible. VERIFIED on synthetic data 2026-08-18: intervening only in periods 1-3 of a 6-period grid returns density ratios of exactly 1.000 at every quantile in periods 4, 5 and 6, so the unintervened periods multiply into the cumulative weight without changing it and cost nothing in positivity. The exposure column for periods 4-6 is a constant 0: there is no therapy to intervene on and the shift leaves it untouched. Verify the learner stack tolerates a zero-variance predictor before committing; SL.glm does.
time._post_window_covariates_why: PI decision 2026-08-18. Periods 4-6 introduce NO new covariates. time_vary is passed as list(L1, L2, L3, NULL, NULL, NULL), which R/Vars.R:18 permits (types = c('NULL','character')) and which was verified to run. The alternative was to compute genuine worst-value covariates over the wide post-window periods, but a 'worst value over day 7 to 14' is a materially coarser variable than a 24h node covariate and pretending the two are comparable is worse than carrying the last node forward and saying so. COUPLING TO k, AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: this works because with k = Inf the outcome regressions at periods 4-6 still condition on the full history including the node-3 covariates. Under a truncated k those periods would condition on NOTHING, since their own time_vary entries are NULL. If k is ever truncated for stability, the carry forward must instead be implemented as explicit duplicated columns. Measured on synthetic data: estimate 0.5822 at k = Inf against 0.5664 at k = 1.

outcome._definition: In-hospital by construction: death is taken from discharge disposition (expired OR hospice), so post-discharge deaths are unobservable. Hospice counts as a death (2.7% at the coordinating site). death_dttm is missing for 37% of counted deaths and the last vital sign is the fallback timestamp, which can flip a patient across the 30-day boundary. ALL OF THIS MUST BE STATED EXPLICITLY IN ANY METHODS SECTION.
outcome._competing_event_how: Via the lmtp `compete` argument. Matches the existing Fine-Gray CIFs in the sibling pipeline's script 05.
outcome._event_time_why: The event time is the discharge that ended the encounter block, NOT clif_patient.death_dttm, which is 37% missing among counted deaths. CLARIFIED 2026-08-18 after this key was misread during implementation of 02: block_discharge_dttm is the source for BOTH events, and 01 therefore emits TWO columns rather than one. days_to_block_end is populated for every block and is when the block ended, whichever event ended it; it is what the competing-risks structure needs, because discharge alive is a competing event rather than an absence of one. death_dttm_by_discharge and days_to_death are masked to deaths and are null for anyone discharged alive; they are what the 30-day mortality definition needs. An earlier single column named event_dttm held the second meaning in its values and invited the first in its name, and 02's first run duly read it the way the name suggested and dropped all 693 survivors from the at-risk set.
outcome._hospice_counts_as_death: 39 blocks at the coordinating site, 2.7% of deaths. A hospice discharge is a transfer OUT of the hospital, not a death in it, so this is a definitional choice that MUST be stated explicitly.
outcome._residual_impossibility: 10 blocks carry a death timed before their CRRT initiation. Same blocks as the Stage 4 late-initiation warning: the contradiction is between the CRRT timestamp and the discharge timestamp in the source, and no choice of event time fixes it. See todo 2e.

_why_this_block: A covariate measurement rule is PROTOCOL, not a site preference. The test is the
one in CLAUDE.md: if two sites set this differently, is the pooled result still
meaningful? If one site pairs a PaO2 with an FiO2 up to 1h old and another up to
24h, P/F is not the same variable and the pooled estimate is not meaningful.
Scripts READ these definitions. They do not decide them. A hardcoded lookback in
a script is invisible to everyone who did not write it and was agreed by nobody.
Settled 2026-08-18 with the PI, covariate by covariate. Supersedes the inherited
fluid_ARDS L_t list, which required urine output and fluid balance.
covariates._source_of_truth: This block is the ONLY place covariate definitions live. The build walkthrough and the site-facing methods document CITE THESE KEYS; they do not restate the values. Two independent statements of one definition drift, and then nobody knows which is the protocol. See .claude/lessons.md, 'The same fact expressed twice is the bug'.

windows._ordering_rule: Every covariate window must END at or BEFORE the start of the exposure node it feeds, so that L_t precedes A_t. L_0 over [-24,0) feeds A_1 over [0,24); node_2 covariates over [0,24) feed A_2 over [24,48); node_3 covariates over [24,48) feed A_3 over [48,72). 02_build_lmtp_df.py ASSERTS window_end <= node_start for every covariate rather than commenting it. The sibling 04_build_causal_df.py violates exactly this rule by pairing a 0-24h mean dose with covariates measured at 24h, and a comment cannot fail.

_excluded_by_decision.cci_score: Components are entered, the composite is not. Entering both double-counts.
_excluded_by_decision.sofa: See _sofa_fallback_parameterisation. Out of the primary set, still computed.
_excluded_by_decision.peep_set: Dropped 2026-08-18. Present in an early draft of the L_t list, removed in the final one.
_excluded_by_decision.calendar_year: Excluded by decision, despite calendar time being the stated reason the study window is protocol.
_excluded_by_decision.race_ethnicity_bmi: Excluded from the nuisance models by decision. Reporting them in a Table 1 is a separate question.
_excluded_by_decision.site: Constant within a federated fit, therefore degenerate as a within-site covariate. Enters at the combination layer as the meta-analysis unit.

pf_ratio.label: PaO2/FiO2 ratio
pf_ratio.algorithm: For EVERY po2_arterial result inside the window, pair it with the most recent non-null fio2_set at or before that result's lab_result_dttm, searching back at most fio2_lookback_hours. Compute pf = po2_arterial / fio2_set. Then take the MINIMUM pf across the window. A window with no po2_arterial, or none that can be paired within the lookback, yields no P/F and falls back to sf_ratio.
pf_ratio._fio2_lookback_why: An FiO2 charted more than 4h before a blood gas is unlikely to describe the conditions that gas was drawn under. Report the share of PaO2 results the cap excludes; if it discards most pairings the cap is wrong and should be revisited before the pilot, not after.
pf_ratio._fio2_scale: fio2_set is on the 0-1 fraction scale at the coordinating site: 3,204,590 of 3,205,294 non-null values are <= 1.0. The 704 values above 1.0 are DROPPED by the clifpy bound [0.21, 1.0], not rescaled to a percentage. The observed maximum of 88,880 gives no basis for guessing intent, and rescaling on a guess would manufacture plausible-looking P/F values out of data entry errors.

sf_ratio.label: SpO2/FiO2 ratio
sf_ratio.role: Fallback for pf_ratio. A SEPARATE COLUMN, never blended into pf_ratio.
sf_ratio.algorithm: Same pairing rule and lookback as pf_ratio, against spo2 instead of po2_arterial, RESTRICTED to spo2 <= 97. Take the minimum across the window.
sf_ratio._spo2_ceiling_why: Above an SpO2 of 97 the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve is flat, so SpO2 carries almost no information about PaO2 and S/F becomes an artefact of how high the FiO2 happens to be.
sf_ratio._why_separate_column: P/F and S/F are different scales. Blending them into one oxygenation column would make the variable's MEANING depend on whether an arterial gas happened to be drawn, and arterial sampling is itself informative because sicker patients get more gases. Carried as two columns plus the pf_source indicator, so the learner sees both the value and its provenance.

pf_source.label: Which oxygenation measure is populated at this node

nee.label: Norepinephrine-equivalent vasopressor dose
nee._coefficients_note: vasopressin's coefficient applies to units/min, not mcg/kg/min. All others apply to mcg/kg/min. NEE conversion factors differ across published sources, which is exactly why they are pinned here rather than left to a script.
nee.algorithm: Standardise doses with clifpy convert_dose_units_by_med_category, using find_most_recent_weight for weight-based units. Build a STEP FUNCTION per drug: an infusion rate is held from each record until the next rate change or stop. Sum the concurrent contributions of all six drugs at every change point inside the window. Take the MAXIMUM of that summed series over the window.
nee.summary: max of the summed step function
nee._hold_hours_why: An infusion rate is held forward from each record for at most 4 hours. Needed because concurrent drugs are not charted at the same instants, so without a hold the sum would understate combined pressor load whenever two drugs were charted minutes apart. Bounded at 4h because the measured median interval between consecutive records of a single vasopressor at the coordinating site is 57 minutes (p90 68 minutes): a silence of four hours is far outside normal charting and most likely means the infusion ended without a stop being charted. mar_action_category == 'stop' sets the rate to 0 explicitly, so the hold only has to cover charting gaps, not real stops. ADDED 2026-08-18 during implementation of 02; it is a protocol parameter because two sites holding rates for different durations would compute different NEE.
nee._stop_signal: mar_action_category == 'stop' sets the rate to zero rather than leaving it missing. Verified present at the coordinating site: 94,759 stop rows across the eight vasoactive categories.
nee._why_step_function: A naive maximum over individual rows takes the largest single-drug dose and so UNDERSTATES combined pressor load: a patient on moderate doses of three agents is sicker than one on a slightly higher dose of one, and the row-wise maximum cannot see the difference.

inotrope.label: Inotrope running at any point in the window
inotrope.algorithm: 1 if either drug has a non-zero rate at any point inside the window, else 0.
inotrope._why_not_in_nee: Dobutamine and milrinone are inotropes, not vasopressors; folding them into a norepinephrine-equivalent sum would misrepresent both. Carried alongside NEE so the cardiogenic phenotype, which has a different tolerance for fluid removal, is not invisible to the model.

lactate.label: Lactate
lactate.algorithm: Take the MAX of all lactate results inside the window.

potassium.label: Potassium
potassium.algorithm: Take the MAX of all potassium results inside the window.
potassium._why: Maximum only, a single term. Hyperkalaemia is an indication for dialysis; a min-and-max pair was considered and dropped to keep the term count down, which is the same concern that drives the node-2 positivity risk.

bicarbonate.label: Serum bicarbonate
bicarbonate.algorithm: Take the MIN of all bicarbonate results inside the window.
bicarbonate._why: Minimum, since lower is worse. The lab_category 'sodium_bicarbonate' (57,435 rows at the coordinating site) is a different quantity and is NOT included.

bun.label: Blood urea nitrogen
bun.algorithm: Take the MAX of all bun results inside the window.

ph.label: Blood pH
ph.algorithm: Prefer ph_arterial. Use ph_venous ONLY if no ph_arterial result falls inside the window; record which was used in ph_source. Take the MINIMUM across the window of whichever source is used.
ph._why_min: Acidosis is the indication for dialysis; alkalosis on CRRT is a consequence of buffer delivery and drives far less clinical action.
ph._why_indicator_not_correction: Venous pH runs roughly 0.03-0.05 below arterial. Silently pooling the two would manufacture an acidosis gradient that tracks SAMPLING PRACTICE rather than physiology. Applying a fixed correction would be worse, since the offset varies with perfusion, which is precisely what is abnormal in this cohort.

ph_source.label: Which pH source populated this node

creatinine.label: Serum creatinine at CRRT initiation
creatinine.algorithm: Take the LAST creatinine result strictly before t0, within creatinine_lookback_hours.
creatinine._why_last_not_extremum: What matters is renal state AT INITIATION, before CRRT begins clearing creatinine. A minimum or maximum over the preceding day would describe the trajectory rather than the starting point.
creatinine._why_baseline_only: After t0, creatinine is largely a readout of delivered clearance, so as a time-varying covariate it is closer to a mediator than a confounder. BUN is retained time-varying because catabolism contributes to it independently of dose.

imv_status.label: Invasive mechanical ventilation in effect
imv_status.algorithm: Run clifpy process_resp_support_waterfall, then take the LAST KNOWN device_category at or before the window's END boundary. 1 if it is 'IMV', else 0.
imv_status._why_boundary_not_any: A point-in-time state at the boundary is what precedes the next exposure node. 'Any IMV during the window' would be a different variable, closer to a severity summary than to the patient's state when the next dose decision is made.

cci_components.label: Charlson comorbidity components, six entered as binaries
cci_components.algorithm: clifpy calculate_cci(hierarchy=True) over the diagnoses of ALL hospitalizations in the encounter block, i.e. at BLOCK GRAIN, exactly as the ESRD exclusion does. All 17 components are computed; six are entered. cci_score is computed and retained for description but is NOT entered.
cci_components._grain_note: Block grain, not hospitalization grain. A comorbidity coded on any hospitalization in a stitched block belongs to the patient for the whole block.
cci_components._no_absorption_target: CONSEQUENCE OF NOT ENTERING cci_score. The inherited per-site prevalence floor rule absorbs a component that fails the floor at any site INTO cci_score, so the covariate set stays identical across sites. With cci_score not entered there is no absorption target, so a component failing anywhere must simply be dropped everywhere. Metastatic solid tumour is the most likely casualty. Fix the floor value before any outcome model is fit, not after seeing prevalences.
cci_components._entered_names_are_clifpy_names: These are the EXACT column names clifpy calculate_cci() emits, not our own labels. Naming them anything else would force the script to fuzzy-match config labels against library output, which fails silently the moment clifpy renames a column. Verified against clifpy 0.4.9, whose 17 components are: aids, cancer, cerebrovascular_disease, chronic_pulmonary_disease, congestive_heart_failure, connective_tissue_disease, dementia, diabetes_uncomplicated, diabetes_with_complications, hemiplegia, metastatic_solid_tumor, mild_liver_disease, moderate_severe_liver_disease, myocardial_infarction, peptic_ulcer_disease, peripheral_vascular_disease, renal_disease.
cci_components._diabetes_lumping_why: clifpy splits diabetes into uncomplicated and with-complications, and hierarchy=True makes them mutually exclusive, so a single 'diabetes' term is the maximum of the two. Lumped because diabetes is carried as a vascular and severity marker rather than for a diabetes-specific mechanism, and splitting it would spend a covariate on a distinction this design does not use.
cci_components._liver_is_moderate_severe_only: mild_liver_disease is NOT entered. hierarchy=True already makes mild and moderate-severe mutually exclusive, so this is a clean split, and mild disease carries little of the fluid-handling relevance that motivated including liver.

weight_kg.label: Weight at CRRT initiation
weight_kg._why_entered: Also the exposure denominator. Entered so the learner can pick up weight dependence that a mL/kg/hr exposure does not encode, and because the actual-versus-ideal-weight question means part of the dose contrast may be adiposity rather than delivered therapy.

outlier_bounds.covariates: .venv .../clifpy/schemas/outlier_config.yaml, applied via clifpy apply_outlier_handling. Pinned by clifpy==0.4.9.
outlier_bounds.exposure_flows: config/outlier_config.json, vendored and byte-pinned at SHA ee4774b.
outlier_bounds._why_two_sources: The vendored config has no bounds for po2_arterial, ph_arterial, ph_venous, bicarbonate, potassium, bun or creatinine. Adding them would edit a file that tests/test_vendor_integrity.py holds byte-identical to the sibling repo, breaking the vendor contract and the dose reconciliation in one move. clifpy already ships consortium-standard bounds for every lab needed, so covariates read from there and the exposure flows keep the pinned file.

missing_values.time_varying: If a covariate has no qualifying observation in its window it is NA at that node, then LOCF from the previous node (from baseline for node 2). Every fill is recorded in a parallel *_locf flag.
missing_values._absence_means_zero_why: For a continuously infused MEDICATION, the absence of a record does not mean the value was not measured; it means the drug was not running. Carrying the previous node's vasopressor dose forward into a node with no infusion recorded would invent pressor exposure for a patient who had been weaned off it, and would do so most often in exactly the recovering patients whose liberation already drives the S1/S2 difference. These variables are therefore set to 0 for every at-risk node with no record, and are NOT eligible for LOCF. Labs are the opposite case: an unmeasured potassium is unknown, not zero, so labs do use LOCF. ADDED 2026-08-18 during implementation of 02, after the first run reported nee 17% and inotrope 84% 'missing' at node 1, which was absence being mislabelled as ignorance.
missing_values.baseline: Left NA by 02. Imputation (MICE) belongs with the fit in 03, not with dataset construction.
missing_values.reporting: Missingness is reported PER VARIABLE PER NODE BEFORE LOCF, so the extent of filling is visible rather than silent.
missing_values._source: LOCF for later time points is Diaz's convention; see fluid_ARDS/plans/analysis_plan.md S4.4.

covariates._volume_assessment_LIMITATION: THIS ANALYSIS HAS NO VOLUME ASSESSMENT OF ANY KIND, patient-side or machine-side. Urine output and fluid balance are unavailable: there is no intake_output table in CLIF at the coordinating site and no urine-output category in vitals or patient assessments, and this is not expected to change soon. crrt_therapy.ultrafiltration_out, the machine-side alternative, is excluded as unstable in this CLIF version (PI, 2026-08-18). SUPERSEDES the earlier text that made urine output and fluid balance a REQUIREMENT for L_t: that requirement was inherited from fluid_ARDS, where urine output is a COMPONENT OF THE EXPOSURE (net fluid balance) and must be lagged for that reason. Here the exposure is CRRT effluent dose, so the rationale does not transfer, and as written the requirement could not be met by any CLIF site. CONSEQUENCE, and it must be stated in any Methods text: the S1/S2 bracket differs precisely because of CRRT liberation, liberation tracks renal recovery, and recovery is now adjusted for only indirectly through BUN, creatinine at baseline, and the severity covariates. The residual confounding direction is known in advance rather than hypothetical.

_sofa_fallback_parameterisation.primary: The granular covariate set above, with no SOFA term.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation.fallback: Non-renal SOFA replacing {pf_ratio, sf_ratio, nee, imv_status, creatinine}.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation.trigger: TO BE FIXED BEFORE ANY OUTCOME MODEL IS FIT. A positivity criterion at node 2 (density-ratio or trimmed-fraction threshold), never the effect estimate.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation._why_sofa_is_not_primary: Two reasons, both the PI's. Entering SOFA total alongside its own subcomponents double-counts. And SOFA's renal component is creatinine-based, so in a cohort where every patient is on CRRT it is near-constant and partly determined by the exposure itself, making it insensitive to the variation this study is about.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation._why_kept_as_a_fallback: Covariate count is what drives the node-2 positivity risk already on record (A2 | A1 near-deterministic, r = 0.75). Non-renal SOFA is a ready dimension reduction if the density ratio proves too sharp. NOT pure compression: it also introduces platelets, bilirubin and GCS, which the granular set does not carry.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation._build_consequence: 02 emits non-renal SOFA and its components REGARDLESS, since they are free from the same compute_sofa_polars call. 03 can then switch parameterisation without rebuilding the dataset.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation._fill_na_scores_with_zero: MUST be False. The clifpy default of True scores a missing component as 0, i.e. normal, which at sparse nodes biases severity downward exactly where data are thinnest.
_sofa_fallback_parameterisation._nonrenal_sum_requires_all_components: sofa_nonrenal is the sum of the five non-renal components and is NULL unless ALL five are present. Summing what happens to be available would reintroduce, through the back door, precisely the bias that fill_na_scores_with_zero=False was set to avoid: a missing component would contribute 0 and read as normal.

estimation._why_sdr: Diaz's own applied choice. See fluid_ARDS/plans/lmtp_discussion.md S6.3 for the real tradeoff against TMLE.
estimation._positivity_check_node2: Fit the node-2 treatment mechanism BOTH WITH AND WITHOUT bicarbonate, and compare the density-ratio distributions. Bicarbonate, potassium and BUN are all cleared or manipulated by CRRT, so at nodes 2 and 3 they are partly a readout of A_1. That is legitimate for L_t, since a time-varying confounder affected by prior treatment is exactly what LMTP handles, but it sharpens the conditional density ratio and feeds the recorded residual risk that A2 | A1 is near-deterministic (r = 0.75). This is a diagnostic, not a covariate-selection rule: do not drop bicarbonate on the basis of the effect estimate.
estimation._diagnostics_why: CHANGED 2026-08-18. This key previously named lmtp_gcomp and lmtp_ipw. Both are DEFUNCT in lmtp: they live in R/defunct.R and call lifecycle::deprecate_stop(), so they raise an error rather than a warning, and they were removed in 1.5.0. No reachable version of the package offers them, because 1.5.0 is also the version that added the competing-risks support this design depends on. The package's own message: 'IPW requires the use of correctly pre-specified parametric models for valid statistical inference. Use lmtp_tmle() or lmtp_sdr() instead.' The replacement diagnostics are what the package actually supports and what the recorded positivity risk needs: agreement between the SDR primary and the TMLE secondary, and the density-ratio distribution plus trimmed fraction read off the fitted object's density_ratios matrix (n x tau).

site_admission._replaces: The `high-dose arm < 100 patients` convention used by the point-treatment analysis, which excluded two sites.
site_admission._why: Outcome-blind and pre-fit. It also readmits the two sites the old rule excluded: under an MTP their support is among the BEST in the consortium (1.3% and 0.4% unsupported; max density ratio 5.5 and 2.1). They are low-dose sites already near the floor, so they contribute little to the contrast, but excluding them was never the right description of that. This inversion is a reportable methodological point in its own right.
site_admission._threshold_todo: Not yet specified. Must be fixed and committed BEFORE any pooled effect is estimated under it.

cohort._definition_source_history: Originally planned as a verbatim vendoring of 00_cohort.py from CLIF-epidemiology-of-CRRT @ ee4774b. Changed 2026-08-16: that file is a converted Jupyter notebook (55 cells, ~900 lines of diagnostics, no callable API), and clifpy 0.4.9 already provides stitch_encounters, compute_sofa_polars, create_wide_dataset and apply_outlier_handling. Reimplemented lean on clifpy primitives instead.
cohort._must_reconcile:
The cohort is intended to match the sibling CJASN analysis. Two papers from the same consortium must not report two different Ns without a stated reason. Because the logic is reimplemented rather than copied, equality is a CLAIM TO BE TESTED, not a fact.

REFERENCE: the sibling pipeline's own STROBE output, CLIF-epidemiology-of-CRRT/output/final_no_phi/crrt_epi/{SITE}_strobe_counts.csv, which is regenerated whenever that pipeline runs. Do not hardcode a target here; read it from that file, so the comparison tracks the reference rather than a snapshot of it.

STANDING AT THE COORDINATING SITE (2026-08-18): this pipeline gives 2,144 blocks against the sibling's 2,145 (4_encounter_blocks_with_weight). One block of the difference is the documented ESRD-grain divergence in esrd_exclusion._known_divergence_from_sibling, where we implement the sibling's stated intent rather than its output. Any further divergence at any site should be explained before results are reported.

An earlier version of this field named 2,136 as the expected count. That figure was the UCMC row of the feasibility audit's tier-1 dose-percentile table, i.e. how many blocks appeared in one audit CSV built from an older vintage of the sibling's intermediate_phi. It was never a cohort definition and should not have been treated as a target.

cohort._stitch_why: Hospitalizations for the same patient separated by less than this gap are treated as one encounter block, the unit of analysis. 6 hours is clifpy's default and the sibling CJASN analysis uses it. PROTOCOL, not site config: two sites stitching at different intervals would be counting different things, and the ED-to-inpatient transfer pattern this exists to absorb is common everywhere.

esrd_exclusion._why: Pre-existing end-stage renal disease is excluded because the study is about CRRT for ACUTE kidney injury. A dialysis-dependent patient's CRRT is not treating AKI, and dose has a different meaning for them. PROTOCOL: the code list defines who is in the study, so it cannot vary by site.
esrd_exclusion._grain: Applied at ENCOUNTER BLOCK grain. If any hospitalization in a stitched block carries an ESRD code, the whole block is excluded; otherwise the partner hospitalization leaks back into the non-ESRD denominator. Pre-existing ESRD is a PATIENT fact, not a hospitalization fact.
esrd_exclusion._known_divergence_from_sibling: This yields 906 excluded / 2,246 remaining at the coordinating site, against the sibling pipeline's 905 / 2,247. Verified 2026-08-17: the difference is the single multi-hospitalization block, where the NON-CRRT partner carries the ESRD code. The sibling's comment states the intent we implement ('if ANY hospitalization in a stitched block has an ESRD code, the whole block is excluded'), but its diagnosis frame was narrowed to cohort hospitalizations before the ESRD lookup, so the partner's codes were never visible. We match their intent, not their output. Downstream reconciliation targets shift by 1 accordingly.
esrd_exclusion._code_normalization: Match on diagnosis_code lowercased with dots removed, so 'N18.6' and 'n186' both hit.
esrd_exclusion._poa_rule: Require present-on-admission, since the exclusion is for PRE-EXISTING disease. But if poa_present carries no positive values at all (some ETLs leave it unpopulated, e.g. the MIMIC conversion sets it to 0 on every row), the POA condition would silently exclude NOBODY and the cohort would just come out larger. In that case fall back to matching on code alone and say so loudly.

cohort._exclude_short_crrt_why: Dropped. It only ever existed because a point-treatment design needs 24h of therapy to define the exposure. LMTP handles early death structurally, so the exclusion is no longer motivated and would now induce selection.

_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.decision: CRRT liberation is neither a competing event nor censoring. It is an exposure value of zero, left unshifted by the policy.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_not_competing: A competing event is one that precludes the outcome. Liberation from CRRT does not preclude in-hospital death; liberated patients remain at risk and some die. The compete argument is correctly occupied by discharge alive, which does preclude in-hospital death.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_not_censoring: Censoring liberated patients would estimate the effect in a world where nobody is liberated within 72h, which is not the question asked. It would also break Assumption 1 positivity for recovering patients, whose probability of remaining on therapy approaches zero.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_safe: The self-limiting shift d(a) = a - delta if a - delta >= floor else a leaves zero unchanged, since 0 - delta < floor for every delta in the ladder. The policy can therefore never move a patient onto or off therapy, only change the intensity of therapy already being delivered. This is what makes dose = 0 an admissible exposure value rather than a covert 'dose or no dose' contrast.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.supersedes: The carry_forward_zero option was previously annotated as silently changing the estimand to 'dose or no dose'. That concern applies to a shift that could push a nonzero dose to zero or lift a zero to nonzero. The self-limiting shift does neither, so the concern does not apply here.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.interaction_with_node_statistic: Follows directly: a charted zero-dose interval enters the time-weighted mean at zero, pulling the node value down, which is the correct behaviour for a delivered-dose exposure. An uncharted gap does not enter at all. Decided once for all zero-dose intervals regardless of cause: liberation, SCUF-only intervals, machine downtime, filter clotting.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.sources_read: Diaz, Williams, Hoffman, Schenck, JASA 2023, pp.1-6 (vector-valued exposure A_t = (A_1t, A_2t) with censoring intervened to 1, p.850; Assumption 1). lmtp R package manual v1.5.4, pp.1-8 and 12-15 (cens mandatory for survival outcomes; compete separate and only for outcome_type='survival'). NOT AVAILABLE in the references folder: Young et al. 2020 and Diaz, Hoffman, Hejazi 2023, both of which bear on competing risks; read them before the competing-event framing is finalised in the manuscript.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.scuf_within_the_window: FULLY RESOLVED 2026-08-18. The cohort script no longer filters by modality at all: a row counts as delivering therapy if any dose-eligible flow is present and positive, which SCUF can never satisfy (verified: 0 of 4,660 SCUF rows have one). So SCUF needs no special case, and a SCUF interval is simply an interval at dose 0. The self-limiting shift already leaves dose 0 unchanged, since 0 - delta < floor. The node statistic now answers the remaining question: the time-weighted mean INCLUDES charted zeros, giving 'clearance delivered over the interval'. Note the mean does not share the median's pathology of returning a value never received: mean([30,30,0,0]) = 15 is the genuine average delivery rate over those four hours. Measured 2026-08-17: 128 of 2,246 blocks (5.7%) have SCUF inside their 0-72h window, median 2 rows, max 66. This is the SAME question as a dose gap from liberation, machine downtime, or filter clotting, so decide it once for all zero-dose intervals rather than per cause.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.scuf_before_t0: Related but separate. 342 blocks have SCUF plus another mode and are retained; only 3 blocks that are SCUF for their entire record are dropped. For those 342 the index event is the first DOSE-ELIGIBLE record, so t=0 sits later than the first CRRT record by a median of 0.6h, but by more than 24h for 18 blocks and by 61 days in one case. Defensible, since SCUF for volume overload and CVVHD for AKI clearance are different therapies for different indications, but it should be a stated choice rather than a side effect of filter placement.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED._coverage_consequence: Treating zero-dose intervals as dose 0 rather than excluding them INCREASES the unshifted fraction, because the self-limiting shift leaves anything below floor+delta untouched (below 20 at delta=5, floor=15). Coverage is the estimand-dilution risk the feasibility audit flags as a headline diagnostic, so report the shifted fraction with the zero-dose intervals included.

_intervention_horizon_OPEN.status: OPEN, raised 2026-08-18 by the PI, deferred pending a closer read of Diaz 2024. BLOCKS nothing already built, but must be answered BEFORE 03_lmtp_fit.R is written, because it decides what the estimand is.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.question: Should the policy intervene only in periods 1-3 (the first 72h), as currently recorded, or at every period where CRRT dose is defined, through day 30?
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.why_it_came_up: Diaz, Hoffman & Hejazi, Lifetime Data Analysis 2024;30:213-236 (the competing-risks LMTP paper, intubation delay with death as the competing event) never encounters the exposure/outcome grid mismatch that forced our 6-period grid. The PI noticed this and was right. The reason is that Diaz's exposure is DAILY MAXIMUM RESPIRATORY SUPPORT, defined and intervened on at every t (section 4.2 p.228; intervention eq. 9 p.229; Fig. 1 p.229 spans days 1-14). His exposure grid and outcome grid are the same object, so tau is the same for both and there is nothing to merge.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.the_real_point: Our asymmetry is a DESIGN CHOICE, not a data limitation. CRRT dose keeps existing past 72h for patients still on therapy. The intervention was capped at tau=3 on positivity grounds (retention >=38% at 48h, thin at 72h at one site; see time._tau_why). Diaz never had to make that call. So the 6-period grid is not a workaround for a package limitation, it is the price of intervening over a shorter horizon than we follow.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.option_A_current: Intervene in periods 1-3 only. Estimand: a 72-hour dose policy followed to day 30. Costs nothing beyond what is built; matches the feasibility audit.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.option_B: Intervene at all 6 periods, structurally identical to Diaz. Requires lifting 01's EXPOSURE_WINDOW_H = 72h cap and auditing positivity past 72h, never done. Likely near-inert in practice: liberated patients sit at dose 0 and the self-limiting shift leaves 0 unshifted, so it buys a wider-sounding estimand for very little actual intervention.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.option_C: A primary, B as a pre-specified sensitivity showing the estimate does not depend on where the intervention horizon is cut. Most defensible, most work.
_intervention_horizon_OPEN.the_substantive_question: Is the policy we mean 'reduce dose for the first 72 hours' or 'reduce dose for as long as the patient is on CRRT'? Different interventions, different clinical readings. Not a technical choice.
